subject: MSA + Order Form: downstream commercialization & training gating
messages:
From: Samuel Chen <samuel.chen@olivetec.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@olivetec.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MSA redline: downstream commercialization and model training questions

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to start the contract thread and surface a couple of items their legal team flagged during an initial read of the MSA + Order Form. High level: Olive is comfortable with standard hosting SLA language, but we need clarity on two IP points before procurement will move to signatures:

1) Downstream commercialization: our product team wants explicit assurance that outputs generated by the service that are used to build derivative features inside Olive will not be treated as Redwood-owned. Specifically: are we assigning any ownership to trained models or downstream product artifacts?

2) Model training / feedback license: Olive wants an opt-out path so their customer data (and any feedback) is excluded from model training unless explicitly agreed. They asked for a short clause in the Order Form to that effect.

I attached the MSA as marked by Olivetec legal (they used track changes). Can you confirm who on your side should be looped in for legal redlines? We want to keep this tight — procurement target is signature by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Sam
Procurement Lead | Olive Technologies

Attachment: Olivetec_MSA_marked.docx (tracked changes)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Chen <samuel.chen@olivetec.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redline: downstream commercialization and model training questions

Sam —

Appreciate the clarity. Looping in Karthik (AE) and Rishi (legal) to triage. Quick notes from our side:
- We do not take ownership of customer outputs in the generic sense — customers retain rights to their content. However, some customers request productization carveouts that allow them to build new product features with derived artifacts; that is negotiable in the Order Form.
- For training, Redwood’s baseline stance is: customer data may be used to improve models unless an opt-out is selected; we can offer an opt-out checkbox on the Order Form (and a stronger contractual commitment in the MSA/Order Form for enterprise deals).

Rishi / Karthik: can you confirm whether a short Order Form line that disallows use for training (and an optional exhibited carveout for downstream productization) will satisfy Olive? Also note: if we grant an opt-out for training, we usually compensate with a pricing uplift or commit to a different availability window for model updates.

I'll keep this thread as the single source for the redline file — Sam, please provide the tracked MSA and the Order Form redlines as separate attachments if possible.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Samuel Chen <samuel.chen@olivetec.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redline: downstream commercialization and model training questions

Marissa / Karthik / Sam —

Thanks for the context — reading Olive's markups now. High-level legal positions I propose for negotiation (short bullets to keep procurement moving):

1) Outputs and derivative artifacts: add an Order Form Exhibit A (Productization Rights) that can be toggled per Order Form. Default: customer retains all rights to outputs they provide to the Service and to any downstream derivative features they build. If customer wants Redwood to have rights to their derivatives for model improvement or broader productization, that must be explicitly listed in Exhibit A.

2) Training / feedback license: offer two options in the Order Form:
   - Opt-in (default): Redwood may use customer data/feedback to improve models, with telemetry redaction and aggregation safeguards.
   - Opt-out: Redwood will not use customer data for training. This is a contractual promise in the Order Form; it will be accompanied by a modest price delta (proposed +10–15%) and a 90-day lag on access to model improvements for that customer.

3) Evidence & auditability: if Olive requires proof that data was excluded from training, we can offer periodic attestations and scoped logs (subject to security/access terms). There are operational costs for long-retention logs — we should surface that to procurement.

Sam: would Olive accept an Order Form with a clear Exhibit for "Training Opt-out" and a short Productization Exhibit that Olive can check to allow any downstream commercialization? If so, we can prepare a redline bundle (MSA + Order Form) and circulate.

Attachment: draft_exhibitA_template.docx (proposed language)

-Rishi
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Chen <samuel.chen@olivetec.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redline: downstream commercialization and model training questions

Sam —

Following up with a concrete proposal so procurement has something to route to legal quickly:

1) Order Form checkbox: "Exclude Olive data from Redwood model training" (if checked, Redwood will not use uploaded data for model improvement; price adjustment +12%).

2) Exhibit B (Productization Carveout): default is unchecked. If Olive wants to claim downstream commercial rights for outputs and derivatives, they check Exhibit B and we add a one-line grant: "Customer retains all rights to outputs and may independently productize derivatives; Redwood will not assert ownership over customer derivatives unless specifically noted in Exhibit B."

3) For auditability, we propose a quarterly attestation and a shared S3 bucket with a hashed manifest for training exclusions (operationally limited to 12 months retention unless otherwise agreed). Cost for extended retention: by quote.

I can convert these bullets into a tracked redline bundle and share a Google Doc. If that approach looks good to Olive we can aim for signature by next Friday.

Next steps: Sam — confirm whether Olive prefers the opt-out as a one-time checkbox on this Order Form or as a company-level setting. If company-level, we'd need procurement to sign that off separately and adjust PS/ops intake.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Related link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Olive-MSA-Redline (draft sent to legal)
Attachment: OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf

From: Samuel Chen <samuel.chen@olivetec.com>

Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redline: downstream commercialization and model training questions

Marissa / Karthik / Rishi —

Thanks — that proposal is exactly the kind of configurable approach Olive prefers. A few clarifying items from procurement/legal:

• The opt-out checkbox on the Order Form is acceptable for this deployment; Olive will check it for the first purchase.
• We want the Exhibit B (Productization Carveout) to be a positive checkbox for Olive to assert downstream rights (i.e., default is Olive keeps outputs but cannot claim rights to change Redwood's models). Can Redwood confirm the exact language for Exhibit B so our legal can run a quick review?
• For attestations/log retention, Olive needs a short SLA for the attestations (response time <10 business days). Can Redwood confirm the retention window for the manifest and a cost estimate for 12 vs 24 months?

If you can circulate the tracked MSA + Order Form redline with the Exhibit wording today, we will route to our GC and procurement and push to signature. Thanks for the rapid turnaround.

Best,
Sam
Procurement Lead | Olive Technologies
